title: Number bonds that make 10
examples: What are the number bonds to 10?
What do I add to 6 to make 10?

explain.say: Here is a puzzle. You have 7 mangoes and your basket holds 10. How many more fit? Look at the ten frame: 7 counters, then 3 new ones fill it up. 7 and 3 make 10!
Pairs that make 10 are called number bonds to 10. A bond is a link, like two friends holding hands. See the 6 counters and the 4 new ones? 6 and 4 make 10. Can you see they fill every box?
Now look: 9 counters leave just one empty box. So 9 and 1 make 10. The more you have, the fewer you need. Which number goes with 8?
Here is a special one: 5 and 5 make 10. The top row and the bottom row are both full, so it is a double! Can you say all the pairs? 0 and 10, 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5.
Brilliant! Here 2 and 8 make 10. Once you know these pairs by heart, sums feel instant. Try this: hold up 3 fingers. How many are still down? That is the bond!

faq.a: A number bond is a pair of numbers that join to make a total. 7 and 3 are a number bond to 10, because 7 plus 3 equals 10.

faq.q: What are all the number bonds to 10?
faq.a: They are 0 and 10, 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, and 5 and 5. You can swap each pair, so 3 and 7 is the same bond as 7 and 3.

faq.q: What do I add to 6 to make 10?
faq.a: Add 4. On a ten frame, 6 counters leave 4 empty boxes, and filling them makes 10.
They make adding and taking away fast. If you know 7 and 3 make 10, you also know 10 take away 3 is 7, and 17 plus 3 is 20.
asks: Why should I learn number bonds?

faq.q: How can my fingers help with number bonds?
faq.a: You have 10 fingers. Hold some up, and the fingers still down are the other part. 4 up means 6 down, so 4 and 6 make 10.
asks: Can I use my fingers for bonds?

facts: Without counting swapped pairs twice, there are 6 number bonds to 10: 0+10, 1+9, 2+8, 3+7, 4+6 and 5+5.
Number bonds are a key part of early maths in Singapore, England and many other countries.
